hero.title: Prioritize Essential Features.
hero.intro: Use the MVP scope from Lesson 41 to prioritise essential features for one customer task. Keep evidence, dependencies, safeguards and deferrals visible.

fields.label: MVP task, customer/context and scope reference from Lesson 41
Evidence/assumption basis, prototype limits and unresolved Validate conditions
Candidate feature list: feature ID, customer task, proposed benefit and source/status
Priority matrix: feature ID | Must/Should/Could/Defer | reason | effort unknown/range | dependency | evidence status
Smallest essential set and why the core task or safety/accessibility needs it
Deferred/excluded features, trade-offs and what would justify revisiting them
Acceptance criteria, essential dependencies/safeguards and checks before implementation
Owner/time boundary, unresolved questions and input for Lesson 43 user flow
Did founder preference or feature popularity override the scoped task?
Which dependency, contradiction or smaller essential set could change your priorities?
Which essential safeguard, effort unknown or Validate condition blocks implementation?

sections.label: 01 / WATCH
sections.heading: Which features are essential for the MVP task?

scenes.title: Use the MVP scope
scenes.narration: Start with the MVP scope from Lesson 41. Keep one customer task, learning question and execution conditions visible. Feature priority serves that task; it is not a popularity contest.

scenes.title: List candidate features
scenes.narration: List features with the task each supports and the evidence or assumption behind it. Do not call an attractive feature necessary just because the founder likes it.

scenes.title: Classify priorities
scenes.narration: Must means the scoped task cannot work responsibly without it. Should matters but can wait for the first version. Could is optional. Defer is outside this build or needs evidence. These are reasoned choices, not a generated score.

scenes.title: Check dependencies and safeguards
scenes.narration: A visible feature may depend on navigation, data handling or accessibility work. Do not defer essential safeguards to make the build look smaller. Mark effort and feasibility unknown until reviewed.

scenes.title: Choose the essential set
scenes.narration: For a registration-route mock-up, a clear entry and destination screen may be essential to the task. Loyalty points can be deferred. Real payment remains excluded. This is fictional planning, not a tested product.

scenes.title: Prepare the matrix
scenes.narration: Write the feature matrix with reasons, effort status, dependencies and acceptance checks. Preserve deferrals and contradictions. Lesson 43 uses the essential set to map the customer experience. No live product is changed.

sections.label: 02 / LEARN
sections.heading: Make the core task work before adding extras.

children: Feature:
a capability that supports a task.
Priority:
its importance within this MVP scope.
Dependency:
work needed before a feature can function.
Deferral:
an explicit decision to leave work outside this version.
Objective:
select a smallest adequate feature set with reasons, dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Why it matters:
a long feature list spreads effort and obscures the core customer task.
Review Lesson 41 MVP scope and Validate conditions manually.
List candidates with task, evidence/assumption and source status.
Classify Must, Should, Could or Defer with reasons.
Check essential dependencies, safety, data handling and accessibility.
Keep effort unknown until reviewed; document trade-offs.
Pass the essential set and acceptance criteria to Lesson 43.
Fictional example

Registration-route mock-up: clear entry and correct destination are Must for the scoped task. A route explanation may be Should if the task works without it. Decorative animation is Could. Loyalty points and actual payment are Defer/excluded. Keyboard access to the core route is essential, not an optional extra. No customer validation or effort estimate is established.

Must is scoped necessity, not market proof. Avoid a numeric total that hides unknowns. A feature can be popular yet irrelevant to this task. Review real technical/security/privacy obligations with responsible owners before execution.
Review Lesson 41 MVP scope

blocks.prompt: Practice: a decorative feature is attractive but unnecessary to the scoped task.

options.label: Mark Must because it looks good
options.feedback: Attractiveness alone does not make a feature essential.

options.label: Keep optional/deferred with a reason
options.feedback: Keep it optional or deferred with a scoped reason; preserve essential safeguards.

children: Complete the eight fields, including a row per feature in the matrix. Example row: F01 | Must | core route entry | effort unknown | destination screen | proposed, not tested. Keep actual evidence unknown where absent.
Local autosave only; plaintext browser storage. Use anonymous planning notes.
Fixed scripted demonstration; no AI/backend. Cannot verify feasibility, permissions, evidence or readiness.
